messages:
Cheng: Quick summary from the mini GPTQ bake I ran this morning across Llama-2-13B / Mistral-7B / Qwen-7B. Used our baseline GPTQ recipe + a small KV-aware correction. High-level: mixed accuracy deltas, some surprising wins on Qwen. Logs and numbers below.

Alex: Nice — top-line numbers?

Cheng: Paste of top-line (average over 3 seeds, eval set = truthbench-lite):
```
model            | fp16 acc | gptq acc | delta
Llama-2-13B      | 78.3     | 77.2     | -1.1
Mistral-7B       | 75.0     | 72.6     | -2.4
Qwen-7B          | 70.8     | 71.5     | +0.7
```
Note: deltas are percentage points. Qwen seems +0.7 here (small but consistent).

Eva: +0.7 on Qwen is interesting — could be tokenization or calibration. Did you use our shared tokenizer align patch?

Cheng: Yes, used tokenizer-align v2. Also added the small KV precision clamp for attention keys (the same tweak we tried in the KV drift experiment).

Maria: What about latency / memory tradeoffs? Any runtime numbers for the GPTQ builds vs fp16?

Cheng: Quick perf snapshot on c5g-hosted small cluster (3 requests, seq=512):
```
model            | fp16 latency(ms) | gptq latency(ms) | VRAM(fp16) | VRAM(gptq)
Llama-2-13B      | 210              | 170              | 23GB       | 12GB
Mistral-7B       | 180              | 160              | 20GB       | 11GB
Qwen-7B          | 220              | 165              | 24GB       | 12GB
```
Throughput improved ~20-30% and VRAM ~45-50% savings.

Alex: Good. Are the accuracy drops for Mistral concentrated on specific tasks (e.g., code/math)?

Cheng: Yes — drift concentrated on math QA and multi-hop reasoning. Natural language QA less impacted. Sample diff shows hallucination uptick on chain-of-thought prompts.

Eva: Can you paste an example failure case?

Cheng: Sure — short snippet (gold vs gptq):
```
prompt: "If A implies B and B implies C, does A imply C? Explain."
fp16: "Yes — by transitivity..."
gptq: "Usually yes, but depends on context..."  <-- more hedging, lower score on truthbench logic metric
```

Maria: Ok. Actionable next steps?

Cheng: Proposal:
- Run AWQ and INT8 profiles for Mistral-7B (to see if different quant family reduces math delta)
- Expand eval set for Qwen to confirm the +0.7 isn't a fluke (add GSM8K, MMLU slices)
- Run KV stress test for long context (4k) to check cache precision degradation
- Canary rollout plan if we ship GPTQ for Qwen: 5% traffic, dedicated pool, monitor perplexity + truthbench set every 10k requests

Bakebot: Canary recipe saved: `canary/qwen-gptq-v1` (policy: 5% steady, auto-rollback threshold: >1.5pp drop on truthbench 1k window).

Devbot: Recommend starting AWQ sweep with these flags: `--awq-scale 0.8 --group-size 32 --kv-clamp 1e-3` and add `--seed 42/43/44` for reproducibility.

Alex: Timeline? How long for AWQ/INT8 sweep?

Cheng: AWQ quick sweep ~6 hours on 8 GPUs, INT8 slower due to retrace ~10-12 hours. Expanded evals add ~4 hours. I can kick off tonight.

Eva: If AWQ recovers Mistral math we should prefer it — better latency than int8 in our stacks. Otherwise fallback to fp16 for math-heavy customers.

Maria: Also add a small A/B prompt set that checks chain-of-thought calibration — alert on >2pp drop.

Cheng: Will run sweeps, push results into the quant-bakes dashboard, and drop a follow-up thread with summarized top candidates + deploy recs.

Alex: Thanks — please cc @platform-ops when canary recipe is ready.

Cheng: Will do. cc:@platform-ops :+1: 

Eva: Nice work, Cheng. Short-term: prioritize Mistral math regression triage and Qwen confirmation.

Cheng: On it.
